note: THE MIGRATION BACKLOG. Every row is a bus verb that writes a plugin DTO store and has no CommandEventBridge channel -- neither a `case` arm nor an `ELEMENT_UPDATE_VERBS` row. SHRINK-ONLY: a verb leaves this file in the same commit that gives it a channel (or removes its plugin-store write). Rows with kind "UNMIRRORED" are DEFECTS with a row, not exemptions. A row whose reason still begins "SEEDED BACKLOG" has NOT been investigated -- that text is a placeholder, and replacing it with a measured sentence is the first half of closing the row. See tools/ga-gate/check-mirror-completeness.ts.

Fix = a case in CommandEventBridge.ts + a subscriber in initTools.ts, OR replace this text with the measured reason it needs neither.

MEASURED AND DELIBERATELY NOT MIRRORED (lane MIRROR3, 2026-08-23). `UpdateSlabHandler` does `Object.assign(slab, updates)` — an OPEN field set, so no ELEMENT_UPDATE_VERBS row can enumerate what it may write, and the whole point of that table is that a field crosses only when somebody established it must. Blocked on the POLYGON SPELLING SPLIT: the plugin record holds `boundary` as `{x,y,z}[]` (world) and the legacy record holds `polygon` as `{x,y}[]` (plan, y = world Z). Until those are one shape, or this verb is narrowed to a declared field list, it stays here.

MEASURED AND DELIBERATELY NOT MIRRORED (lane MIRROR3, 2026-08-23). Same polygon spelling split as `slab.update`: `boundary` `{x,y,z}[]` (plugin, world) vs `polygon` `{x,y}[]` (legacy, plan with y = world Z). The translation is writable — `vec3RingsToPlanRings` in `elementUpdatedMirror.ts` already does it for `holes` — but a POLYGON move must also re-seat everything hosted on the slab, which `UpdateSlabPolygonCommand` does and a field copy does not. Mirroring the ring alone would move the plate out from under its walls.
